name: WEUSD
oneLiner: WEUSD is PicWe's omni-chain wrapper with disputed USDC-vs-USDT/MOVE backing and a recent off-peg market price.
collateral: PicWe's current public docs describe WEUSD as minted and redeemed 1:1 against USDC during Phase 1, while the mint-authority review and earlier PicWe materials describe basket-style backing around 9 USDT + 1 MOVE. Pharos treats the backing model as disputed until PicWe reconciles the documentation with on-chain and market evidence.
pegMechanism: Issuer-operated mint/redeem route through PicWe contracts. Current PicWe docs describe 1:1 USDC mint and redemption, but earlier basket materials and persistent secondary-market pricing near $0.91 indicate unresolved redemption/backing ambiguity.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: At BSC block 110046907, Base block 48645553, Arbitrum block 483958453, and Plume block 81162729 on 2026-07-15, tracked EVM token 0xdd73ea766b80417c0607a3f08e34a0c415d89d56 had a zero EIP-1967 implementation slot and independently verified PicWe_USD source/ABIs limited to ERC20, permit, AccessControl, MINTER_ROLE, and mint. They expose no pause, freeze, blacklist, or arbitrary-holder-burn function, and burnFrom is allowance-gated. Asset-wide false is not supportable because Movement is 465086.702603 of 501682.757399 current listed deployment supply (92.70%). Its PicWe package publishes neither module source nor source map while its WEUSD ABI stores TransferRef and BurnRef; linked mint/redeem and bridge modules expose pause functions, and publisher-compatible package upgrades leave scope and authorization unprovable. Aptos fungible-asset documentation says TransferRef can freeze holders and BurnRef can burn fungible assets. This is bounded direct possible, not a confirmed current all-holder freeze. Issuer documentation did not provide independently verifiable legal terms or proof-of-reserves/transparency attestations.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: WEUSD moves cross-chain via PicWe's own issuer-operated burn-on-source / mint-on-destination route. PicWe's cross-chain-transfer docs state "Source chain burns, target chain mints" over a self-built native bridge ("No Wormhole. No LayerZero. No third-party risk") with PicWe-operated keepers signing and verifying every cross-chain message. On-chain this is confirmed: the EVM token (identical CREATE2 address 0xdd73... on bsc/base/arbitrum/plume) is a plain ERC20 + AccessControl with no LayerZero/Wormhole/OFT interface, so cross-chain mints flow purely through MINTER_ROLE held by a PicWe admin EOA plus the mint/redeem contract, and on Movement through the weusd_cross_chain_gas cross_mint_role_contract relayer (batchMintWeUSDCrossChain). The durable supply path is therefore issuer-native burn/mint, not an external validated network, canonical bridge, or liquidity route. Trust posture is weak: keeper validation has no published external attestation or audit, control keys are concentrated PicWe EOAs with no multisig/timelock, and the token trades off-peg (~$0.91) under disputed backing.

notices.title: Backing disclosure conflict and active depeg
notices.message: WEUSD trades near $0.91 while PicWe's current docs describe 1:1 USDC backing and older PicWe-linked materials describe a roughly 9 USDT + 1 MOVE basket. Treat the peg and redemption model as disputed until PicWe publishes reconciled reserve evidence.

mintAuthority.summary: WEUSD is minted and redeemed through PicWe's omni-chain protocol via AccessControl tokens whose live BSC/Base/Arbitrum roles resolve to a PicWe admin/minter EOA plus a mint/redeem contract; the basket-style backing (roughly 9 USDT + 1 MOVE) explains the persistent ~$0.91 trading level.

controls.label: PicWe WEUSD DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE and MINTER_ROLE holder
controls.evidence: BSC block 103632076: hasRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE) and hasRole(MINTER_ROLE) both returned true; eth_getCode returned empty (EOA confirmed). Same role checks on Base block 47201470 and Plume block 74174478 also returned true. Movement: the Movement contract (0xf39c2674...) uses a different architecture — minting is controlled by the deployer EOA (0xf39c267... auth key = own address, sequence_number = 3, normal EOA) through admin-gated functions in weusd_mint_redeem and weusd_cross_chain_gas modules, consistent with the same PicWe admin.

controls.label: PicWe WEUSD mint/redeem contract (EVM chains)
controls.evidence: BSC block 103632076: hasRole(MINTER_ROLE) returned true. Same check on Base block 47201470 and Plume block 74174478 returned true. No modules or guards detected in EVM Safe API checks.

controls.label: PicWe WEUSD Movement package publisher
controls.evidence: Movement REST reports an authentication key equal to the publishing account and package picwe at upgrade_number 0 with compatible upgrade policy 1. This account can publish compatible replacements for weusd, weusd_mint_redeem, and weusd_cross_chain_gas with no on-chain timelock. The EVM WEUSD contracts on BSC, Base, Arbitrum, and Plume have zero EIP-1967 implementation slots and are not proxies; PicWe's April 2026 directory separately lists the upgradeable investment modules and does not classify the WEUSD core contracts as proxies.

review.evidence: BSC/Base/Arbitrum/Plume role checks confirmed EOA 0xc122... as DEFAULT_ADMIN+MINTER_ROLE holder and mint/redeem contract 0x5D54... as MINTER_ROLE holder; the new PicWe contract directory independently lists the same token and mint/redeem addresses on Arbitrum. EIP-1967 implementation slots are zero on the reviewed EVM contracts. Movement REST reports cross_mint_role_contract 0x86e5136... and a publisher-controlled package with compatible upgrade policy 1. All tracked chains and the distinct Movement upgrade path are resolved; no multisig or timelock was found.
